Abstract.AbstractText: Spiritual nursing care is a fundamental aspect of care often unobserved during students' clinical experiences. A nursing student shares her disillusionment about the lack of spiritual care she observed during a clinical rotation. Her instructor used the negative experience to identify areas for curriculum improvement to develop and address the lack of spiritual nursing care education.

AffiliationInfo.Affiliation: Maureen Kroning, EdD, RN, is a nursing supervisor at Good Samaritan Hospital, Suffern, New York, and an associate professor at Nyack College of Nursing. Her greatest reward is teaching future generations of nurses. Deborah Yoon, BA, is a third-year student at Nyack College, pursuing a BSN degree. She is presently managing a physical rehabilitation clinic and working as patient care assistant at an ambulatory surgery unit.

Article.ArticleTitle: Student Perspective Improves Spiritual Care Curriculum.

Journal.Title: Journal of Christian nursing : a quarterly publication of Nurses Christian Fellowship
